intro: Ignacy Jan Paderewski made this recording of Chopin’s Étude in G♯ minor, Op. 25 No. 6 (Thirds), in 1923, four years after he served as Poland’s prime minister. The piano part calls for fast paired notes in the right hand and a quiet voice.

sections.label: A · Thirds in G♯ minor, sotto voce
sections.mNote: The study opens with a right-hand trill, marked sotto voce.

sections.label: B · Left-hand melody under right-hand thirds
sections.mNote: The left hand plays a slower melody beneath quick right-hand thirds.

sections.label: C · Paired notes across the keyboard
sections.mNote: The right hand plays chromatic scales in paired notes.

sections.label: Coda · The last bars of thirds
sections.mNote: The running pairs draw towards the close

cues.title: Right-hand thirds, sotto voce
cues.text: Chopin marks the étude sotto voce. The right hand plays trills and runs in thirds throughout, two notes sounding together at each step. The left hand has a slower melodic line beneath them.
cues.evidence: Sotto voce and continuous right-hand thirds: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/192. Left-hand melody: Fred Yu, https://www.ourchopin.com/analysis/etude25.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Paderewski in Warsaw and Paris, 1919
cues.text: Crowds cheered Paderewski in Warsaw on New Year’s Day 1919. Two weeks later he became Poland’s prime minister, and that spring he represented the country at the Paris Peace Conference. By February 1920 he had returned to his musical career, and he made this Victor recording in 1923.
cues.evidence: Andrzej Chojnowski, ‘Paderewski, Ignacy Jan’, 1914–1918-online (2014): Warsaw arrival, 16 January premiership, April peace conference and February 1920 return to music. https://encyclopedia.1914-1918-online.net/article/paderewski-ignacy-jan/. Recording year: https://archive.org/details/78_etude-in-g-sharp-minor_ignace-jan-paderewski-chopin_gbia0183841b.

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
